basic_info.name: Dr IA — Sistema de Análise (Grupo Me Indica)
basic_info.category: AI exam interpreter (lab + imaging) with consumer wellness add-ons; not a lab, not telemedicine. Side product of a PLR ebook reseller group
basic_info.stage: Live micro side-project. Core exam-analysis feature in temporary maintenance ('Em manutenção') as of 2026-08; no funding, no press coverage, no Wayback archive history. Built no-code (Lovable) by a solo founder (domain registered 2023-11-15 under an individual CPF)
basic_info.pricing_model: Freemium + credits + ads. Premium subscription R$ 27,99/month (monitoring tools included, priority AI queue). Non-expiring credit packs: 1 credit R$ 5,00; 15 credits R$ 20,00; 50 credits R$ 40,00; 100 credits R$ 70,00. Each AI analysis costs 1 credit; 50 credits can activate 30 days of Premium. New users get a 24-hour free trial then 0 credits (bundle message: 'Seu período de teste grátis de 24 horas expirou e você tem 0 créditos'); after lapse the account falls back to a basic free plan with a monthly exam limit [uncertain: exact free monthly exam quota]. Payments via Stripe checkout. Free/non-premium tier is monetized with Monetag ad scripts. No price-change history found
basic_info.target_user: Lay patients: frequent exam takers, hypertension self-monitors, family caregivers managing relatives' exams and prescriptions, people far from medical centers wanting explanatory triage, prevention/self-care users. A 'Profissional de Saúde' signup role exists but no distinct professional workflow is visible
basic_info.scale_metrics: No published user, revenue, or funding figures; zero press coverage; zero Wayback snapshots. Proxies indicate hobby scale: Instagram @meindica87 has 279 followers (following 1,214), with affiliate/make-money story highlights. Not a durable threat — low-budget template product whose flagship feature is currently switched off. [uncertain: actual user base]

product.core_features: 1) Upload of blood or imaging exams (PDF or photo) for AI simplification into lay language, organized by topics with general wellness recommendations (currently disabled for 'improvements'). 2) Medication tracker with multiple daily schedules and visual calendar. 3) Blood-pressure log with daily measurements, evolution charts and downloadable PDF report. 4) AI calorie calculator: photo of a meal returns estimated calories plus protein/carb/fat breakdown, nutrition history and 30-day PDF report ('Viver Bem' report). 5) Exam history with integrated charts
product.signature_differentiator: Nothing defensible. Closest to unique: bundling imaging-exam interpretation (X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG) with blood-work interpretation in one cheap consumer tool, plus a user-facing AI model selector (Gemini 1.5 Flash/Pro, gemini-2.0-flash-exp, GPT-4o, DeepSeek). All of it is off-the-shelf LLM vision calls — the entire prompt and JSON schema are readable in the client bundle (project originally named 'gemini-exam-insights' on Lovable)
product.lab_data_handling: Manual upload only: digital reports or phone photos of printed exams; vision models read image/text and extract parameters, units, reference ranges, classifying each item Normal/High/Low/Critical with a didactic explanation. No lab integrations, no ordering, no retest cadence, no hardware, no wearables. Prompt includes the user's last 3 analyses as history context
product.family_dependents_depth: Shallow. 'Family caregivers' are a marketing persona only — no dependent accounts, no pediatric reference ranges, no hereditary-risk logic (no 'dependente' string exists anywhere in the app bundle)
product.doctor_sharing: Minimal: blood-pressure and calorie PDF reports formatted 'to hand directly to your doctor', with copy suggesting sending by email/WhatsApp or printing. No share links, no doctor portal, no consultation brief, no SOAP; 'Profissional de Saúde' is only a signup radio button
product.action_loop_monetization: Post-interpretation loop is generic wellness advice plus in-house monitoring tools (meds, BP, calories) — no supplement store, no protocols, no telemedicine, no prescriptions, no marketplace. Monetization is upfront (Stripe subscription/credits) plus Monetag display ads shown to non-premium users on a health-data product

technology.ai_approach: Direct calls to consumer LLM APIs with a hardcoded Portuguese prompt requesting structured JSON (parameters, values, units, reference_range, status Normal/Alto/Baixo/Crítico, clinical_significance). Multi-model: default 'gemini_padrao' = gemini-1.5-flash; options include gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-2.0-flash-exp, gpt-4o, deepseek-chat. No proprietary clinical engine, no human-in-the-loop review, no fine-tuning evidence. Credit debit has a client-side fallback that writes user_credits directly from the browser (security weakness)
technology.data_inputs: Uploaded exam files/photos (blood panels, X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG), manual blood-pressure readings, medication schedules, meal photos
technology.data_interoperability: Input: file/image upload in the web app only. No FHIR, no Apple Health / Health Connect, no RNDS/REL, no LIS/lab integrations, no public API, no WhatsApp ingestion. Exhaust: PDF export (BP and calorie reports). Backend on Supabase (project lptjkrrzyvejadfjywjd.supabase.co) with Realtime websocket; payments via Stripe checkout session
technology.platform: Web app (React/Vite PWA built with Lovable) at dr-ia.grupomeindica.com.br with 'install to home screen' prompt; no native iOS/Android app found, no API

ux.onboarding: Landing page -> signup modal (name, email, 6-char password, profile Patient/Professional) -> 24-hour free trial with credits -> upload exam. Time-to-value in minutes while the feature is up; currently blocked by the maintenance banner on the analysis feature
ux.data_visualization: Blood-pressure evolution charts over time with anomaly framing, integrated exam-history charts, visual medication calendar, nutrition history for the meal calculator. Per-parameter status rendering (Normal/High/Low/Critical); no health score, no trend projections, no reference-band visualizations
ux.engagement_channel: Weak/transactional. PWA install prompt and Supabase realtime only; no push notifications, no email lifecycle, no community, no streaks, no nudges found in the product. Organic social is Instagram/Facebook/X/Pinterest under the Meindica brand (affiliate-marketing tone: 'AFILIADO', 'OPORTUNIDADE', 'VENDER' highlights), not a health community. Retention relies on manual return of caregivers/BP loggers; no WhatsApp channel

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: No accuracy claims beyond marketing ('advanced NLP and computer vision models... excellent second opinion... high contextual precision') — no numbers, no published methodology, no clinical board, no human review. Risks: LLM vision hallucination on medical imaging with no guardrails; imaging claims (fractures, tumors, hemorrhage) marketed to lay users; ad-network scripts (Monetag) running on pages that handle health data; client-side credit handling; parent company has zero healthcare background (PLR ebooks, R$ 1,00 price point, 'CineVault' streaming template reused for legal pages). Transparency: pricing is clear on the plans screen, but free-tier limits are vague
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Positions itself as an educational, non-diagnostic tool with explicit disclaimers ('does not replace a doctor', 'never provides diagnoses') and LGPD claims (end-to-end encryption, irreversible deletion on account closure). No mention of ANVISA / RDC 657/2022 SaMD registration anywhere in the site or bundle; the imaging-analysis claims would likely qualify as software-as-medical-device territory if enforced, but it operates openly as a wellness/education tool with no visible regulatory engagement
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they do NOT do (opportunities for Dr. Exame): no lab integrations or broad ingestion (FHIR/RNDS/Health Connect); no dependents/caregiver accounts with pediatric ranges; no doctor-facing portal, share links or consultation brief; no longitudinal biomarker trends or reference bands; no hereditary/family risk layer; no WhatsApp retention channel; no human-in-the-loop review; no published methodology. What works (inspiration, not copy): bundling multiple cheap wellness tools (meds, BP, meal photo) around the exam hook to lift frequency; the caregiver persona is well-articulated on the landing page; per-parameter Normal/High/Low/Critical status is instantly legible for lay users
trust_gaps.relevance: Medium-low. Category overlap is direct (BR, AI second opinion + exam simplification, includes imaging interpretation which Dr. Exame does not do), but execution is a solo, no-code, ad-monetized side project with the flagship feature currently offline and ~zero traction (279 IG followers). Monitor quarterly at most; the durable BR threats are the funded players, not this
